title: macOS Kernel Panic Generic
shortDescription: Generic macOS kernel panic from the 0x80100000 prefix.
fullDescription: macOS shows the 'Your computer restarted because of a problem' banner and the panic log lands in /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports. Most panics in this range come from third-party kernel extensions (kexts), failing RAM on Intel Macs, or buggy Thunderbolt/USB-C docks on Apple Silicon.

causes.cause: Outdated macOS build missing Apple-side fix

symptoms: 0x80100000 reported in Console.app or a system dialog
Issue reproduces after reboot
Related crash reports in /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports
Problem clears temporarily after clearing caches

fixSteps.title: Reboot and reproduce
fixSteps.instruction: Restart the Mac normally and reproduce the issue. Capture the exact error string from Console.app > 'All Messages'.

fixSteps.title: Update macOS
fixSteps.instruction: System Settings > General > Software Update. Install all available updates.

fixSteps.title: Boot into Safe Mode
fixSteps.instruction: Intel: hold Shift at boot. Apple Silicon: shut down, hold Power until 'Options', select startup disk while holding Shift.

fixSteps.title: Reset relevant subsystem
fixSteps.instruction: If the code relates to power/thermal: reset SMC. If it relates to display/startup disk: reset NVRAM. If iCloud: sign out and back in.

fixSteps.title: Run Apple Diagnostics
fixSteps.instruction: Intel: hold D at boot. Apple Silicon: boot to Options and press Cmd+D. Review reference codes and escalate hardware failures to Apple.

whenToCallPro: Apple Support or Genius Bar — in-warranty Macs get free diagnosis; AppleCare covers repair after hardware tests fail.

faq.a: Not usually. Try software fixes (update, Safe Mode, cache reset) first. Apple Diagnostics confirms hardware failures.
Software fixes are non-destructive. Before advanced steps (reinstall, erase), make a Time Machine backup.
